scope.summary: Define the canonical versioned BodyPose pin/contact authority consumed by BodyKit IK, multi-actor poses, PoseKit lift, props, cloth, and animation.
acceptance_criteria: Registers hsk.tailor.body_pose_contact_set@1 as the single contact/pin schema; MT-519..521 and interlink consumers import it and must not define a second ContactConstraint type.

Every constraint declares actor/entity/effector ids, frame and local transforms, direction, positional and angular tolerances, equality/unilateral/contact mode, priority, weight, compliance, friction with units, active timebase, authored-versus-inferred provenance, and collision exception policy.

Validation rejects unresolved actors/effectors, non-finite values, incompatible frames, negative tolerances/compliance/friction, invalid intervals, contradictory hard constraints, and contact sets whose source binding is stale.
Pins and contacts are immutable proposal inputs until the canonical BodyPose apply command explicitly commits them with expected-base, actor, lease, event, and receipt attribution.

Immutable BodyPoseContactSet payloads are content-addressed ArtifactStore artifacts linked by EventLedger events and indexed through guarded BodyKit storage; list/get/replay reverify schema/content/source hashes and preserve authored/inferred provenance.
scope.risk_if_missed: Duplicate or underspecified contact types would make multi-actor posing, cloth collision, and PoseKit-derived proposals disagree about the same physical relationship.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Non-UI scope: behavior is observable through typed Tailor state, receipts, captures, diagnostics, and TraceProjection; the owning native-shell MT verifies GUI projection.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > PoseKit and character-sheet interlinking

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
